title: Defining Ethically Sourced Code Generation
findings: Religion is identified as an aspect of 'Social Acceptability', one of the 11 dimensions of Ethically Sourced Code Generation (ES-CODEGEN). The paper suggests developers should ensure that the inputs, outputs, and development processes of CodeGen models align with religious principles, citing examples like Halal certification (Islam) and ethical concerns from religious communities about vaccines derived from aborted fetal cell lines (often associated with Christianity). However, survey results indicate that 'Social Acceptability' is among the dimensions practitioners are most likely to ignore, despite acknowledging its relevance.
